content.text:
I submitted **index 2 (Sb fraction 0.256)** as the best composition. It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.0198%. That is still very low in absolute terms.

All 5 EQE measurements are spent; I didn't use any of the XRD budget.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.150 | 0.0144 |
| **2** | **0.256** | **0.0198** |
| 4 | 0.324 | 0.0098 |
| 14 | 0.502 | 0.0009 |
| 23 | 0.680 | 0.0003 |

- **Pb-rich end wins:** EQE drops as Sb goes up. The Sb-rich samples near the two known mixed phases (Pb₂Sb₂O₇ at Sb 0.5 and PbSb₂O₆ at Sb 0.67) came out 10 to 100 times lower.
- **Why it's low overall:** the band-gap model (MEGNet) predicts about 2.5 eV and 2.7 eV for those two phases. Both are above the 2.1 eV illumination, so these films should absorb little of the light. I didn't run it on any Pb-rich phase, so I can't say why that end does better.
- **Where the true peak could be:** somewhere between Sb 0.15 and 0.32. I never measured index 1 (Sb 0.195) or index 3 (Sb 0.286), so one of them could beat index 2.
- **Last measurement:** the fitted model's top pick was index 5 (Sb 0.37). I measured index 4 instead, as a compromise between exploring further and checking next to the best result.
